rationale: Hebrews 11:13 (BSB) says that Abraham and the other patriarchs 'acknowledged that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.' 'Acknowledged' (Greek ὁμολογήσαντες) points to something they said, and Genesis 23:4 is where Abraham says it of himself: 'I am a foreigner and an outsider among you.' Many commentators on Bible Hub's Hebrews 11:13 page name this verse. The Expositor's Greek Testament: the confession 'was made no doubt by their whole conduct, but as the aorist indicates it was made verbally by Abraham on the occasion of Sarah's death (Genesis 23:4).' The Pulpit Commentary: 'The reference is to the confession of Abraham to the sons of Heth (Genesis 23:4).' Meyer, Barnes, Bengel, the Cambridge Bible, Ellicott and MacLaren also cite it, several of them alongside Jacob's words to Pharaoh (Genesis 47:9). The Greek agrees only in part. The Septuagint of Genesis 23:4 has πάροικος καὶ παρεπίδημος; Hebrews has ξένοι καὶ παρεπίδημοι in every edition Bible Hub shows, so only the second noun is shared. This row follows conn-matt5-psalm37-meek: a near match with no citation formula is an allusion. It is graded strong because of the 'acknowledged' marker, the shared παρεπίδημος and the breadth of commentators who name 23:4. It is not graded explicit because Hebrews names no scene and Jacob's words are a second candidate. Hebrews 11:9-10 (living 'as a stranger in a foreign country') already belongs to conn-gen12-call-hebrews11-8 and is not repeated here.
